title: What If Sarawak Was Its Own Kingdom?
notes: Same rules as E01. Real history up to 1963; from scene 3 everything is fiction. Ending is deliberately a food debate (kolo mee vs laksa), not a political poll.

scenes.name: The Hook
scenes.visuals: Golden-hour Kuching: camera tilts down from the sky to a (fictional) coronation — Queen Auntie waves from the palace balcony, fireworks, hornbill-and-chopsticks flags. Hard cut to an airport immigration counter: 'Next! IC, please.' STAMP. Caption: real fact — Sarawak already runs its own immigration checks.

scenes.name: Real History
scenes.visuals: REAL HISTORY badge. Parchment timeline: Brooke era ends 1946 → British Crown Colony. Regional map: Malaya, Singapore, Sabah and Sarawak light up together — '16 SEPT 1963 · MALAYSIA FORMED' (small note: Singapore separated in 1965). Sarawak piece wiggles: 'went solo?'

scenes.name: The Kingdom (fiction)
scenes.visuals: ALTERNATE HISTORY — FICTION banner. Sarawak piece floats free and is stamped 'KINGDOM OF SARAWAK (fictional)'. The National Kolo Mee Cook-off: flaming woks, scoreboard, judges. Auntie wins; a crown drops onto her head; confetti; 'LONG LIVE QUEEN AUNTIE'.

scenes.name: Royal Decree
scenes.visuals: Throne room styled like a golden kopitiam. The Premier asks for the first decree; the Queen bangs the table: 'Fix. The. Road. Lah!' Decree scroll unrolls. Road crew fills the pothole in one sparkle — FIXED ✓. Card: 'NEXT DAY'. A new pothole pops up right beside it; a car bounces.

scenes.name: Ringgit Sarawak
scenes.visuals: A banknote spins in: RINGGIT SARAWAK with Queen Auntie's portrait and a hornbill watermark (all fictional). Money-changer board: '1 RS = 1 BOWL OF KOLO MEE ▲'. Queen at her stall, outraged at the price board.

scenes.name: Balik Kampung
scenes.visuals: Departure board: KUCHING → KUALA LUMPUR · INTERNATIONAL. Grandma video-calls from the Peninsula. Family group chat renamed '(diplomatic channel)', messages pop in with visa stamps.

scenes.name: Reality Check
scenes.visuals: Population counter ≈2.5 million (Census 2020: 2.45 million). A balance scale: OWN BUDGET on one pan; OWN BILLS on the other — army, airports, hospitals, embassies — tipping back and forth, unresolved.

scenes.name: Final Punchline
scenes.visuals: Night market: the Queen, crown on, back at her kolo mee stall with a queue. 'One great war…' — kolo mee vs laksa VS screen with lightning. End card: KOLO MEE 🍜 or LAKSA 🍲? COMMENT BELOW 👇. Camera tilts up into the golden sky that opens the video (loop).

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: What if Sarawak... was its own kingdom?
lines.tts: What if [Sarawak](/səɹˈɑːwak/)... was its own kingdom?

lines.speaker: officer
lines.text: Next! IC, please.
lines.tts: Next! I. C., please.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Plot twist: Sarawak already runs its own immigration checks.
lines.tts: Plot twist. [Sarawak](/səɹˈɑːwak/) already runs its own immigration checks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Real history: in 1946, Sarawak became a British Crown Colony.
lines.tts: Real history. In nineteen forty-six, [Sarawak](/səɹˈɑːwak/) became a British Crown Colony.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then in 1963, Sarawak, Sabah, Malaya and Singapore formed Malaysia.
lines.tts: Then in nineteen sixty-three, [Sarawak](/səɹˈɑːwak/), [Sabah](/sˈɑːbɑː/), Malaya and Singapore formed Malaysia.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But what if Sarawak... went solo?
lines.tts: But what if [Sarawak](/səɹˈɑːwak/)... went solo?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In this made-up timeline, Sarawak becomes its own kingdom.
lines.tts: In this made-up timeline, [Sarawak](/səɹˈɑːwak/) becomes its own kingdom.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And the monarch? Picked every ten years... by a kolo mee cook-off!
lines.tts: And the monarch? Picked every ten years... by a [kolo mee](/kˈoʊloʊ mˈiː/) cook-off!

lines.speaker: queen
lines.text: Aiyo! I win ah?
lines.tts: [Aiyo](/aɪjˈoʊ/)! I win ah?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Long live Queen Auntie!
lines.tts: Long live, Queen Auntie!

lines.speaker: minister
lines.text: Your Majesty, your first royal decree?
lines.tts: Your Majesty... your first royal decree?

lines.speaker: queen
lines.text: Fix. The. Road. LAH!
lines.tts: Fix. The. Road. Lah!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Finally! The road is fixed...
lines.tts: Finally! The road is fixed...

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: ...for one whole day.
lines.tts: for one whole day.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: New kingdom, new money: the Ringgit Sarawak.
lines.tts: New kingdom, new money. The [Ringgit](/ɹˈɪŋɡɪt/) [Sarawak](/səɹˈɑːwak/).

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Official exchange rate? One note... one bowl of kolo mee.
lines.tts: Official exchange rate? One note... one bowl of [kolo mee](/kˈoʊloʊ mˈiː/).

lines.speaker: queen
lines.text: Price go up again? Who approve?!
lines.tts: Price go up again? Who approve?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Going back to the Peninsula for the holidays? That's international travel now.
lines.tts: Going back to the Peninsula for the holidays? That's international travel now.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Come home for the holidays... and bring your passport!
lines.tts: Come home for the holidays... and bring your passport!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The family group chat is now a diplomatic channel.
lines.tts: The family group chat is now... a diplomatic channel.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But would a kingdom of about two and a half million people really be better off?
lines.tts: But would a kingdom of about two and a half million people, really be better off?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: More say over its own money... but also every bill to pay by itself.
lines.tts: More say over its own money... but also, every bill to pay by itself.

lines.speaker: queen
lines.text: Royal duties done. Now, back to my stall!
lines.tts: Royal duties done. Now, back to my stall!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Kingdom or not, Sarawak would still fight one great war...
lines.tts: Kingdom or not, [Sarawak](/səɹˈɑːwak/) would still fight one great war...

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Kolo mee, or laksa? Comment below!
lines.tts: [Kolo mee](/kˈoʊloʊ mˈiː/)... or [laksa](/lˈʌksə/)? Comment below!
